title: Dynamic SRE Part 1: Breakpoint Rebellion
description: Climb four floors of a reverse-engineering tower filled with binary digits, disassembly screens, register banks, and memory circuits. Complete nine ordered Dynamic SRE Part 1 checkpoints, then reach the congratulations room on Floor 4.

nodes.text: Welcome to Floor 1 of the AVALANCHE reverse-engineering tower. Collect the exercise at Mission Briefing, match the C-code comments, then identify the IDA string reference. Work individually and keep the exercise PDF open. Each scored checkpoint unlocks the next.

Follow the lower corridor to the right, go up along the right edge, then return left along the upper corridor. The glowing lift at tile 4,7 takes you to Floor 2. Floor 2 covers breakpoints and registers; Floor 3 covers the stack, patching, and debrief; Floor 4 is the congratulations room.

Welcome to Floor 2. Trace the print call, predict the branch for the exercise’s incorrect input, then inspect eax at the strcmp breakpoint. Use the exercise’s debugging steps between the scored checkpoints. Watch what changes each time execution advances.
Follow the same lower-right-upper-left route. The upper-left lift takes you to Floor 3. To return to Floor 1, step off your purple arrival tile and then back onto it.

Welcome to Floor 3. Identify the other strcmp argument on the stack, apply the binary patch, and verify the result from Cygwin. Then complete the individual debrief. The Uber Challenge remains optional. Submit your one–two paragraph write-up through the course email process using subject Assignment-DynReverse1; entering OK does not send it.

Complete the three checkpoints along the lower-right-upper-left route. After your debrief, take the upper-left lift to Floor 4 and celebrate. To return to Floor 2, step off your purple arrival tile and then back onto it.

Congratulations You Completed the Assignment! You climbed from source code to disassembly, live execution, memory, and binary patching. Welcome to Floor 4. The whole analysis crew is cheering for you!
Enjoy the trophies and binary light displays. To return to Floor 3, step off the purple arrival lift and then back onto it. Keep your exercise and notes for Part 2.
Well done! You used breakpoints to slow execution, followed branches, and identified the values passed to strcmp. That careful observation is what turns assembly into evidence.
A breakpoint gives you time to ask what changed, where it is stored, and what the next instruction will do. Great work practicing those questions.
Great work! You changed the branch behavior, applied the patch to the binary, and checked it outside the debugger. Enjoy the trophy hall!
Your individual debrief is submitted through the course email process. Once that is sent, celebrate your completed mission.
